Two potential formats that could work well depending on goals:

**Option 1: Dataset Discovery & Processing**

This mirrors the IRW work we do but as a collaborative sprint where participants:

-Identify public Spanish-language survey datasets from Latin America (government statistical agencies, World Bank, LAPOP, etc.)

-Build Python/R/Stata files to standardize and process them into long-format tables

-Create respective metadata (construct names, descriptions, context texts in English/Spanish)

-Document the entire pipeline for reproducibility

This would also increase our library and give participants experience with data curation standards. Output could be 5-10 fully processed datasets ready for the IRW.

**Option 2: Research Methods & Analysis Hackathon**

Use existing datasets from the IRW as starting points for participants to:

-Develop research questions and test analytical approaches (nonparametric tests, indices, visualizations, etc.)

-Write brief research methods papers or technical notes documenting their findings

-Experiment with different econometric/statistical techniques on the same data

-Present preliminary findings and lessons learned

> **Depends on:** #2, #7

## Background / Context

Right now the app only ever renders hackathons as cards on the Home page (`frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx` maps over the list into `frontend/src/components/HackathonCard.tsx`). There is no per-hackathon page, so there is nowhere to show full information, no shareable URL for a single hackathon, and nowhere to hang future features like Q&A and change-requests. `react-router-dom` is already wired up in `frontend/src/App.tsx` (it currently declares only `/` and `/feedback`), so adding another route is low-friction.

This issue adds a detail route at `/hackathon/:id` that displays every field of a hackathon and makes each card link to it.

## Goal

Add a per-hackathon detail page at a stable, shareable URL (`/hackathon/:id`) that shows all fields of a hackathon plus a placeholder slot for Q&A, and make `HackathonCard.tsx` navigate to it.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create a new page component `frontend/src/pages/HackathonDetail.tsx`.
- [ ] Register the route `/hackathon/:id` in `frontend/src/App.tsx` (alongside the existing `/` and `/feedback` routes), pointing at the new page.
- [ ] Read the `:id` route param with `useParams` and resolve the hackathon. Use the data-access helper from the **frontend-api** issue (do not call `fetch` directly here, and do not re-read `localStorage`/`sampleHackathons` in this component). Conceptually this resolves a single record via `GET /api/hackathons/:id`, which is owned by **backend-api** (server side) — this page only consumes it through the shared client.
- [ ] Render all fields from the canonical `Hackathon` type (see **data-model**): `name` (as the page heading/title), `description`, `startDate` and `endDate` (ISO 8601, formatted for display), `location`, `mode` (`"in-person" | "online" | "hybrid"`), `organizer`, `tags`, and prize info (`hasPrize` + `prizeDetails`).
- [ ] Render the official link from the `url` field as an external "Visit website" link (`target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`), only when present.
- [ ] Gracefully handle optional fields: only render a field's row/section when it has a value (every field except `id`, `name`, and `status` is optional in the canonical model). Treat an empty-string `location` (`""`) the same as omitted — per **data-model**, `location: ""` is normalized to omitted, so do not render an empty location row.
- [ ] Add a placeholder section for Q&A (e.g. a heading "Questions" with a short "Coming soon" note). Do not implement Q&A logic here — it is owned by the **qa-comments** issue, which builds on `GET/POST /api/hackathons/:id/questions`.
- [ ] Make `frontend/src/components/HackathonCard.tsx` link the card to `/hackathon/:id` (use react-router `Link` / `useNavigate`). Keep the existing external-link icon pointing at `url`; the card body / title should be the internal navigation target so clicking the card opens the detail page.
- [ ] Add a "not found" state: if no hackathon matches `:id`, show a friendly message and a link back to Home (`/`).
- [ ] Reuse the existing shadcn/ui primitives in `frontend/src/components/ui/` (e.g. `card.tsx`, `button.tsx`) and Tailwind classes so the page matches the rest of the site.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visiting `/hackathon/:id` for a known id renders a page showing `name`, `description`, `startDate`/`endDate`, `location`, `mode`, `organizer`, `tags`, prize info, and the external `url` link when each is present.
- [ ] Clicking a card on Home navigates to that hackathon's detail page, and the browser URL is `/hackathon/<that-id>` (shareable — pasting the URL into a new tab loads the same hackathon).
- [ ] Optional fields that are missing (including an empty-string `location`) do not render empty/broken rows.
- [ ] A Q&A placeholder section is visible on the detail page.
- [ ] Visiting `/hackathon/:id` with an unknown id shows a "not found" message and a working link back to Home.
- [ ] No raw `fetch` calls or direct `localStorage`/`sampleHackathons` reads live in `HackathonDetail.tsx` — data comes through the shared data layer.

## Dependencies

- **data-model** — the page must render the expanded canonical `Hackathon` shape (`name`, `url`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `mode`, `hasPrize`, `tags`, `status`, etc.). Field names used here come from that issue, not the current thin `topic`/`date`/`prize`/`link` shape in `frontend/src/lib/types.ts`.
- **frontend-api** — this page should fetch a single hackathon (conceptually `GET /api/hackathons/:id`, server-side owned by **backend-api**) through the shared client so it works the same whether data is local or from the backend.

## Out of scope / notes

- Implementing Q&A behavior, posting questions/answers, or the change-request flow — those are separate issues. Q&A is owned by **qa-comments** (`GET/POST /api/hackathons/:id/questions`, `POST /api/questions/:id/answers`); the change-request flow's backend (`POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request`) is owned by **backend-api** with the "Suggest an edit" UI owned by **change-request**. This page only adds a placeholder slot so those can drop in later.
- SEO (meta tags, social preview, prerender) is a separate follow-up (**seo**); this issue just provides the stable shareable URL `/hackathon/:id` that the SEO work targets.
- `interestCount` is reserved/deferred (populated later via Discord) — do not build UI for it now.
- If the **frontend-api** issue is not yet merged when someone starts this, reading from the same `loadHackathons()`-style local source used in `frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx` is an acceptable temporary stand-in, but keep the lookup behind a helper so swapping to the real API client is a one-line change.
- This issue would benefit from a `frontend` label, which does not exist in the repo yet. Not applied here; recommend maintainers create `frontend` (and the other commonly-requested `backend`/`design` labels).

For YC hackathon

## これまでのGitHub内リサーチ・壁打ちの要約（#2〜#22）

- **#10 Main Idea**: 「エージェントが読める会社の生きた世界モデル」という当初の広い構想から、#18/#19の自己分析を経て「組織横断の承認・レビュー依頼における状態捕捉」という狭いウェッジに絞り込み済み。
- **#18/#19**: 自分自身の実体験（学校の利用規約回付が教員→教頭→法務部の間で追跡不能になった）が原体験。壁打ちで「可視化ではなく捕捉が本質」「発信者の可視性 vs 意思決定者の割り込み削減、2つの痛みを混同していた」という重要な再定義を得た。
- **#20 Problems**: #10を元にした30個の問題を整理済み。
- **#22 Gap**: 競合company-brain.aiは静的なファクト共有止まりで、Capture自動化・Entity Resolution・Interaction/Reasoning Graph・矛盾検知・Action層・Feedback Loopがいずれも弱い、と判明。
- **#13**: YCのRFS（Tom Blomfield）が名指しで「Garry's G-Brainを全企業向けに」と書いており、自分がローカルで動かしている`gbrain`はその個人用リファレンス実装そのもの。
- **#15（4 Builders, One Architecture）**: Karpathy・Garry Tan（GBrain/GStack）・Hannah Stulberg（DoorDash Team OS）・Rampが収斂した共通アーキテクチャは (1) markdownベースの中央ストア (2) RESOLVER.md的なルーティング層 (3) skillsという作業単位 (4) 答えを書き戻す規律 (5) モデルとコンテキストの分離（ベンダーロックインしない）の5要素。かつ実装より「社内導入」の方が難所で、①コンテキスト捕捉に数ヶ月かかる ②何を書き/書かないかのS/N比 ③「置き換えられる／出遅れて見える」という恐怖 ④ハードウェア/セキュリティポリシーの壁 ⑤「監視」に見える懸念、の5つが共通の障害として挙げられている。対策は「draftsのみで人間が必ず承認」「透明性（誰でも中身を読める）」「チーム単位のopt-in」。
- **#16（HyperのHN Launch）**: 競合Hyperの技術詳細（fact=subject-predicate-object、supersession方式で矛盾を解消、provenance+アクセス制御タグ、embeddingsとPostgres全文検索のハイブリッド retrieval）が判明。同時にコメント欄で浮かんだ未解決の批判点: ①ベンダーロックイン・データ主権への懸念（Hyperが潰れたら「石器時代に逆戻り」との指摘）②陳腐化問題は解決されていない（月曜正しくても金曜には黙って古くなる）③fact抽出は親子関係のような複雑な構造を失う ④意図（intent）の捕捉に失敗し、無関係なセッションに古いメモが紛れ込む ⑤「役職による信頼度」のような権威づけがまだ単純（新しい人間の発言を古い発言より信頼、程度）。

## 提出に向けてこれからすべきこと

### 1. スコープと物語の確定（最優先）
- [ ] デモのシナリオを「#18/#19の自分の実体験（部活イベント/利用規約の組織横断承認が迷子になった話）」に固定し、Problem→Solutionの物語をこの一本に絞る。YCは"founder-market fit"（なぜ自分がこれを作るのか）を重視するため、この原体験をピッチの冒頭に据える。
- [ ] #10のオープンな問い（ターゲット顧客: 学校法人/大企業のような階層の深い組織 vs スタートアップ）に決着をつけ、デモ内で扱う組織像を1つに固定する。
- [ ] 発信者の可視性 と 意思決定者の割り込み削減、どちらを一次価値にするかを決定する（#18の指摘）。ハッカソンの尺では両方を作り込む時間はないため、片方に絞る。

### 2. 差別化ポイントの明文化（Gap分析・競合批判点を反映）
- [ ] #22のGap（company-brain.aiは静的ファクト共有止まり）と、#16のHyperへの批判（陳腐化未解決・fact抽出が構造を失う・intent捕捉失敗・ロックイン懸念）を踏まえ、「自分たちは何を捨てて何に集中するか」を1枚のスライドに言語化する。
  - 例: 全社ファクトの網羅ではなく、承認・レビュー依頼という単一の業務プロセスの状態捕捉に絞る。
  - 例: 「追跡コード」という低摩擦な参加手段で、非協力的な関係者（更新をサボる部署）を巻き込む導線を持つ点をHyper/company-brain.aiとの違いとして強調。
  - 例: markdownベースでポータブルな substrate（#15のAFCS思想）を採用し、ベンダーロックイン懸念（#16のHN批判）に正面から答える。

### 3. 技術スタックの決定（スピード優先）
- [ ] #15で判明した共通アーキテクチャ（markdown中央ストア＋RESOLVER.md的ルーティング＋skills＋書き戻し規律）をベースに採用し、ゼロから設計しない。ローカルで実運用実績のある`gbrain`（ontology/schema pack/chronicle/skills）をそのまま基盤として使い、ハッカソンの短時間開発に耐える土台にする。
- [ ] 「追跡コード」を、事実上のエンティティID（#15でいうところの entity system の最小版）として設計し、gbrainのlinks/timeline機能に載せられるか検証する。
- [ ] 矛盾検知・権限管理・Entity Resolutionなどの重い機能は今回のデモではスコープ外と明言し、「捕捉」と「状態追跡」の一本槍に絞る（#15の教訓: 導入の難所は技術より捕捉習慣の定着にある）。

### 4. デモに実装する最小機能（MVP）
- [ ] 追跡コードを発行し、依頼が別の人・別のツール・メールを渡り歩いても状態（受領/レビュー中/差し戻し/完了）が引き継がれる最小フロー。
- [ ] 「今どこで止まっているか」を追跡コードから引ける参照UI（ノードUIは#18の助言通り後回しにし、シンプルな一覧/検索で十分）。
- [ ] 非協力的な関係者でも低摩擦で状態を残せる導線（例: メール返信やSlackメッセージに追跡コードを含めるだけで自動的に状態が更新される）。
- [ ] Drafts-only・人間が必ず承認、というAFCS流の信頼構築パターン（#15）をデモの中で見せ、「監視ツールに見えない」ことを審査員に示す。

### 5. ピッチ・提出物の構成
- [ ] 構成案: 原体験（#18/#19）→ 既存解の限界（#22のGap、#15の導入障壁、#16の未解決課題）→ なぜ今か（#13のYC RFS、#14/#16の競合資金調達が市場の存在を裏付け）→ 解決策のデモ → 差別化（狭いウェッジ＋低摩擦捕捉＋ポータブルな基盤）→ 今後のロードマップ（このウェッジをFactual/Interaction Memory層のデータ源として、#10の当初構想へ将来つなげる）。
- [ ] ハッカソンの提出要件（フォーマット・動画尺・提出フォーム・チーム構成・締切）を再確認し、確定していなければ確認して別途書き出す。
- [ ] リポジトリを公開設定にする必要があるか、審査員向けのREADME/デモ手順を整えるか確認する。

### 6. 想定される審査員からの質問への準備
- [ ] 「company-brain.aiやHyperと何が違うのか」→ #22/#16の比較表をそのまま使えるように整理しておく。
- [ ] 「陳腐化・矛盾検知はどうするのか」（#16 sid_shipsの指摘）→ 今回のスコープでは対象外にしていることを正直に示し、次フェーズの計画として#10のSource Truth層に繋げる説明を用意する。
- [ ] 「非協力的な関係者をどう巻き込むか」（#18/#15共通の最難関）→ 追跡コードの低摩擦設計で答える。

---

## 検討している機能一覧（#10〜#26の全議論から再整理）

これまで各issueに散らばっていた機能アイデアを、レイヤーごとに改めて書き並べる。

### A. 記憶（Memory / Capture）層

1. **追跡コードの発行** — 仕事・相談を始める前に、一意の追跡コード（宅急便の伝票番号のようなもの）を発行する（#19, #26）
2. **追跡コードによる会話の自動収集** — Slack・メールなどのやり取りに追跡コードを付けると、それらを自動的にひとつの「箱」に集約する（#26）
3. **全文保存 + AI要約の並存** — 一次情報の全文を保持しつつAI要約も添える。人間が後から元の発言を確認できるようにし、要約による意味の欠落（特に日本語のニュアンス）に人間が気づけるようにする（#24）
4. **非デジタル情報の捕捉** — 口頭でのやり取り・電話・紙の書類など、データ化されていない情報をVoiceOS/STT（音声認識）や会議録音＋自動要約で拾う（#24）
5. **リアルタイム・ハイブリッド議事録** — 会議中にAIが「ここが意思決定の転換点では」とリアルタイムで提案し、人間が自分の言葉でその場をブックマーク・確定できる（#24）
6. **入力フォーマットは強制しない** — 構造化フォーム（プロンプト形式）と自由記述の両方を用意し、どちらを選ぶかは任意。オンボーディング離脱を防ぐ（#24）
7. **「入力は人間、出力はAI」の原則** — 意思決定の記録・理由づけは人間が自分の言葉で行い、AIはその大量の一次情報を要約・提示するアウトプット側にのみ徹する（#24, #26の反省材料でもある）

### B. 推論（Reasoning）層

8. **決定確定時の自動矛盾チェック** — 承認しようとした瞬間、AIが会社全体の過去の「箱（決定事項）」と照合し、矛盾する過去の決定がないか警告する（例:「昨年、データは30日保持と決めていますが、今回の即時削除で上書きしますか？」）（#26）
9. **Source Truth & 情報源の権威づけ** — どの情報源が「正」なのかの優先順位づけ、情報の鮮度管理（#10）
10. **Interaction / Reasoning Graph** — 決定の理由・対立・前提を構造化して保持する。「何が起きたか」だけでなく「なぜそうなったか」を残す（#10, #24）

### C. 行動（Action）層

11. **決定確定後の自動バトンパス** — 決定が確定すると、次に誰が動くべきかをシステムが判断し、必要な情報を自動的に該当者・チャンネルへ届ける（#26）
12. **Action / Execution** — エージェントが実際にタスクを実行する（Skills/MCP経由）（#10）

### D. 状態追跡・可視化

13. **状態追跡** — 追跡コードをもとに、依頼が今どの段階（受領/レビュー中/差し戻し/完了）にあり、誰が担当しているかを参照できる（#18, #19）
14. **ノードUIによる可視化**（優先度低） — Blenderのノードエディタのような、人と人の繋がり・情報の流れを可視化する画面。捕捉ができた後の提示層として後回しにする（#18の壁打ちの助言）

### E. 基盤・ガバナンス

15. **Entity Resolution** — 同一人物・同一顧客・同一プロジェクトの名寄せ（#10）
16. **Permission** — ワークフロー単位のアクセス制御。個人メモ→チーム記憶→会社記憶への昇格ルール（#10）
17. **Feedback Loop** — 人間の訂正が自動的にルール化され、次回から反映される（#10）
18. **配信方式としてのファイル/MCPサーバー化** — Claude Code/Cursor等どのエージェントからも同じ土台を読める形で提供し、特定ベンダーにロックインしない（#10, #15）

### F. 将来案・優先度が低いもの

19. **パーソナライズされた意思決定モデル** — 特定の意思決定者（経営者等）の考え方をAIに学習させ、本人不在でもその人らしい判断基準を再現する（#24、機能過多の懸念ありのため優先度低）
20. **過去データの取り込み** — 意思決定の文脈が欠落しノイズになりやすいため、優先度は低い、またはスコープ外という論点あり（#24, 他チームの結論。自分たちのgbrain活用前提との整合は要検討）

### 未解決のまま残っている技術的な問い（#26で指摘済み）

- 3の「自動収集」は、コードの手動貼り付け（高摩擦）かNLPによる自動判定（未解決の難問）か、どちらの前提かが未確定。
- 8の「矛盾チェック」は、情報源の権威づけルール（#9 Source Truthの設計）がないと機能しない。
- 11の「自動バトンパス」は、権限・組織図・役割の設計（#16 Permission）が前提として必要。
- 非協力的な関係者を実際にどう巻き込むかの具体策が、上記のどの機能にもまだ組み込まれていない。


---

## ハッカソン発表に向けて、これからすべきこと（#26の決定事項を反映した更新版）

body:
Part of #3381.

## Problems (confirmed in `cognee/infrastructure/llm/config.py`)
1. **Provider specified twice.** `llm_provider="openai"` AND `llm_model="openai/gpt-5-mini"` both encode the provider; `get_llm_client.py` then does `LLMProvider(llm_config.llm_provider)` and dispatches a large if/elif. The provider could be inferred from the model prefix in most cases.
2. **Per-provider instructor mode is scattered across 9 adapter files.** `LLM_INSTRUCTOR_MODE` defaults to `""`, and each adapter hardcodes its own `default_instructor_mode` (gemini→`json_mode`, bedrock→`json_schema_mode`, anthropic→`anthropic_tools`, ollama→`json_mode`, llama_cpp→`JSON`, custom→`json_mode`, …). The documented "gpt-4o uses json_schema_mode" behavior is buried and inconsistent.
3. **Embedding rate-limit fields live in `LLMConfig`** (`embedding_rate_limit_enabled/requests/interval/tokens`) — they belong in `EmbeddingConfig`.
4. **BAML is a full parallel surface** (`baml_llm_provider/model/endpoint/api_key/temperature/api_version`) duplicating the same six concepts behind `STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_FRAMEWORK`.
5. **Fragile quote-stripping allow-list.** `strip_quotes_from_strings` hardcodes 14 field names to strip Docker `--env-file` quotes; every new string field must be added.
6. **LLM config validates embedding config.** `ensure_env_vars_for_ollama` reaches into `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER/MODEL/DIMENSIONS/HUGGINGFACE_TOKENIZER` via raw `os.environ`, only when provider is ollama.

## Proposed simplification
- **Single source of provider truth:** infer provider from `llm_model` prefix when `llm_provider` is unset; deprecate requiring both.
- **One instructor-mode table** mapping (provider/model → mode) in a single module; adapters read from it. Removes 9 scattered defaults.
- **Move embedding rate-limit fields** to `EmbeddingConfig`.
- **Generalize quote-stripping** to all `str` fields via a validator instead of an allow-list.
- **Lift the ollama all-or-nothing check** into a provider-agnostic cross-config validator (covers any provider that needs paired embedding settings).

## Acceptance
- Setting only `LLM_MODEL="anthropic/claude-..."` (no `LLM_PROVIDER`) works.
- Instructor-mode defaults come from one table; removing a hardcoded adapter default doesn't change behavior.
- `embedding_rate_limit_*` accessible from `EmbeddingConfig`.
- No regression for BAML / OpenAI / Azure / Ollama paths.

body:
Part of #3381.

## Problems (confirmed in `embeddings/config.py` + `get_embedding_engine.py`)
1. **Silently defaults to OpenAI when only the LLM is configured.** Two mechanisms:
   - Static defaults `embedding_provider="openai"`, `embedding_model="openai/text-embedding-3-large"` — if you set only LLM env vars, embeddings silently use OpenAI regardless of your LLM choice.
   - Key fallback in the engine factory: `api_key = embedding_api_key or llm_api_key` (with a confusing `custom`-provider tautology at `get_embedding_engine.py:120-121`). The embedder borrows the LLM's key when its own is unset.
   This is the documented "configure only one and the other defaults to OpenAI" footgun — it surfaces as confusing runtime behavior, not a clear error.
2. **`embedding_dimensions` resolution fails silently.** `model_post_init` probes fastembed then `litellm.model_cost`; on miss it logs a warning and uses `_FALLBACK_DIMENSIONS = 3072`. The code comment itself flags this as "the source of the silent `Vector(3072)` mismatch on every non-OpenAI embedder" — the wrong dimension only blows up on first vector write, not at config time.
3. **Dead-branch default:** `embedding_batch_size` both branches return 36 (lines 104-107).
4. **Naming drift:** the field is `embedding_max_completion_tokens`, but docs/people expect `EMBEDDING_MAX_TOKENS`.

## Proposed simplification
- **Make embedding provider derive from the LLM when truly unset, OR require it explicitly — but never silently pick OpenAI.** At minimum, when `LLM_PROVIDER` is non-OpenAI and no embedding provider is set, emit a clear warning/error rather than defaulting to OpenAI.
- **Fail loud on unknown dimensions:** if `embedding_dimensions` can't be resolved and isn't set, raise a config-time error naming the model, instead of defaulting to 3072.
- **Collapse the dead batch-size branch** to a single default.
- **Accept `EMBEDDING_MAX_TOKENS` as an alias** for discoverability.

## Acceptance
- Configuring a non-OpenAI LLM without embedding settings produces a clear message (not a silent OpenAI embedder).
- An unresolvable embedding model fails at config time with an actionable error, not on first write.

body:
## Idea
Cognee's config works but is sprawling and footgun-prone: ~50 LLM env vars, a parallel BAML set, embedding knobs split across two modules, and **three differently-named database config families** that force you to repeat the same Postgres credentials up to three times. This umbrella tracks focused simplifications across LLM, embedding, and database config.

All configs are pydantic `BaseSettings` (`env_file=".env"`, `extra="allow"` → no typo protection), each behind an `@lru_cache` `get_*_config()` singleton, with a parallel `get_*_context_config()` ContextVar layer for multi-tenant overrides. The user-facing setters (`config.set_llm_config`, `set_embedding_config`, `set_relational_db_config`, `set_graph_db_config`, `set_vector_db_config`) mutate the cached singleton in place via `object.__setattr__`, **bypassing validators** (so `fill_derived` won't re-run after a `set_*`).

## Child tickets
- [ ] #3382 — **LLM config**: centralize per-provider instructor-mode defaults (currently scattered across 9 adapters), reconcile provider duplicated in `llm_provider` + `llm_model` prefix, move embedding rate-limit fields out, reduce the BAML parallel surface.
- [ ] #3383 — **Embedding config**: stop silently defaulting to OpenAI when only the LLM is configured; fail loud on unknown `embedding_dimensions` instead of silently using 3072.
- [ ] #3384 — **Database config**: unify the three prefix families (`DB_` / `VECTOR_DB_` / `GRAPH_DATABASE_`) and reconcile provider strings (`postgres` vs `pgvector` vs `postgres_graph`) so the Postgres "everything" combo needs one credential block, not three.

## Cross-cutting fixes worth doing once
- Turn on typo protection (`extra="forbid"` or a warning) — `extra="allow"` silently swallows misspelled env vars.
- Make `set_*_config()` re-run the `model_validator`s so derived fields stay consistent after programmatic config.

## Key files
`cognee/infrastructure/llm/config.py`, `cognee/infrastructure/databases/vector/embeddings/config.py` + `get_embedding_engine.py`, `cognee/infrastructure/databases/{relational,vector,graph}/config.py`, `cognee/api/v1/config/config.py`.

## Hackathon Deliverables

---

## 1 · Project Write-Up _(≤ 200 words)_

**The Problem**

In Southeast Asia — especially the Philippines — crowdfunding is broken. Platforms like Kickstarter hand creators 100 % of funds before a single promise is kept. With high crypto-wallet adoption and a fast-growing creator economy across the region, the cost of broken trust falls entirely on backers.

**What Ember Does**

Ember is a milestone-based, onchain crowdfunding platform built on Morph L2. Contributions are locked in a per-project smart contract. Funds release only when backers vote to approve each milestone — no middlemen, no custodians, no rug pulls.

**Morph L2 Integration**

- **ProjectEscrow** — one immutable Solidity contract per project holds bridged USDT; no upgrade keys
- **PositionNFT** — ERC-721 minted to every backer's wallet as transferable proof of stake
- **On-chain voting** — weighted by USDT contributed; keeper resolves after window closes
- Low-fee, fast-settling transactions accessible to everyday Filipino users

**Why SEA?**

The Philippines leads Southeast Asia in crypto-wallet adoption. Millions of Filipinos already hold USDT for remittances and savings. Ember meets them where they are — a stable coin they know, a mobile-friendly UI, and a crowdfunding model that actually holds creators accountable.

---

## 2 · Architecture Diagram

### C4 — System Context

```mermaid
C4Context
    title Ember — System Context

    Person(backer, "Backer", "Funds projects, votes on milestone releases")
    Person(org, "Organization / Creator", "Creates projects, submits milestone proofs")
    Person(admin, "Super Admin", "Verifies orgs, audits activity logs")

    System(ember, "Ember Platform", "Milestone-based onchain crowdfunding — web app + indexer")

    System_Ext(morph, "Morph L2", "EVM-compatible Layer 2 — escrow contracts, NFTs, USDT")
    System_Ext(wallet, "EVM Wallet", "MetaMask / Reown AppKit — signs and submits transactions")
    System_Ext(email, "Resend", "Transactional email delivery")

    Rel(backer, ember, "Browse, fund, vote")
    Rel(org, ember, "Create projects, submit milestones")
    Rel(admin, ember, "Verify orgs, review audit logs")
    Rel(ember, morph, "Build calldata, read on-chain state")
    Rel(backer, wallet, "Sign transactions")
    Rel(org, wallet, "Sign transactions")
    Rel(wallet, morph, "Submit transactions")
    Rel(ember, email, "Queue notifications")
```

---

### C4 — Container Diagram

```mermaid
C4Container
    title Ember — Containers

    Person(user, "User (Backer / Org / Admin)")

    Container_Boundary(platform, "Ember Platform") {
        Container(web, "Web App", "Next.js 15 (App Router)", "SSR pages, REST API routes, Better Auth, wagmi/Reown for wallet")
        Container(indexer, "Indexer", "Node.js + ethers.js", "Watches on-chain events via WebSocket RPC, syncs DB, enqueues emails")
        ContainerDb(db, "Database", "PostgreSQL + Prisma", "Projects, orgs, milestones, contributions, votes, email log, activity log")
        Container(queue, "Job Queue", "BullMQ + Redis", "Reliable email delivery with retries; cursor-based backfill on restart")
    }

    System_Ext(morph, "Morph L2", "ProjectFactory · ProjectEscrow · PositionNFT (Solidity + OZ v5)")
    System_Ext(resend, "Resend", "Email API")

    Rel(user, web, "HTTPS / WebSocket")
    Rel(web, db, "Prisma ORM")
    Rel(web, morph, "Read-only RPC (wagmi)")
    Rel(indexer, morph, "ethers.js — subscribe to contract events")
    Rel(indexer, db, "Prisma ORM — upsert idempotent rows")
    Rel(indexer, queue, "Enqueue email jobs")
    Rel(queue, resend, "HTTP — deliver email")
```

---

### Sequence — Backer Contributes to a Project

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant B  as Backer
    participant UI as Ember Web (Next.js)
    participant M  as Morph L2 🟣
    participant IX as Indexer
    participant DB as Postgres

    B->>UI: Open project page, enter USDT amount
    UI->>UI: wagmi useSimulateContract — encode contribute()
    B->>M: Wallet signs & submits USDT.approve() + ProjectEscrow.contribute(amount)
    M-->>B: tx confirmed — PositionNFT minted to backer wallet
    M-->>IX: emit Contributed(backer, amount, tokenId, txHash)
    IX->>DB: INSERT Contribution (idempotent on txHash)
    IX->>DB: UPDATE Project.totalRaised (atomic increment)
    IX->>DB: ENQUEUE EmailNotification — CONTRIBUTION_RECEIVED
    DB-->>B: Email: "Your contribution is confirmed"
```

---

### Sequence — Org Submits Milestone → Backers Vote → Funds Released

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant O  as Org Owner
    participant UI as Ember Web (Next.js)
    participant M  as Morph L2 🟣
    participant IX as Indexer
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant B  as Backers

    O->>UI: POST /api/projects/:id/milestones/:mid/submit (updateNote)
    UI-->>O: encoded submitMilestone(index, updateUri) calldata
    O->>M: Wallet signs & submits ProjectEscrow.submitMilestone()
    M-->>IX: emit MilestoneSubmitted(index, updateUri, voteEndAt)
    IX->>DB: UPDATE Milestone — status=VOTING, voteEndAt
    IX->>B: MILESTONE_VOTE_OPEN emails to all backers

    B->>M: Wallet signs & submits ProjectEscrow.vote(index, support)
    M-->>IX: emit Voted(voter, index, support, votingPower)
    IX->>DB: INSERT MilestoneVote (unique on txHash+logIndex)

    note over M,IX: voteEndAt passes — keeper fires every 60 s
    IX->>M: keeper calls ProjectEscrow.resolveMilestone(index)
    M-->>IX: emit MilestoneResolved(index, passed=true)
    IX->>DB: UPDATE Milestone — status=PASSED
    IX->>O: MILESTONE_VOTE_OUTCOME email
    O->>M: Wallet signs & submits ProjectEscrow.claimMilestone(index)
    M-->>O: USDT transferred to org receivingWallet 💸
    M-->>IX: emit MilestoneClaimed(index)
    IX->>DB: UPDATE Milestone — status=CLAIMED
```

---

### Smart Contract Architecture (Morph L2)

```
ProjectFactory (singleton)
│
├─ createProject(milestoneCount, bps[], deliverableDates[])
│      └─ deploys ──▶  ProjectEscrow   (one per project, immutable, no upgrade key)
│                      │  ├─ contribute(amount)           USDT in → PositionNFT out
│                      │  ├─ submitMilestone(index, uri)  org only
│                      │  ├─ vote(index, support)         backers only, weighted
│                      │  ├─ resolveMilestone(index)      anyone after voteEndAt
│                      │  └─ claimMilestone(index)        org only, after PASSED
│                      │
│                      └─ deploys ──▶  PositionNFT (ERC-721)
│                                       └─ tokenURI → /api/nft/:contract/:tokenId
│
└─ emits ProjectCreated(onChainId, escrowAddress, nftAddress)
         └─ indexed by Ember Indexer → sets Project status=LIVE
```

> **Depends on:** #2

## Background / Context

The backend is currently a stub. `backend/main.py` defines only two routes (`/health` and `/ping`) and `backend/requirements.txt` lists just `flask` — there is no database, no persistence, and no real API. Meanwhile the frontend has no API calls at all: it sources hackathons from the hardcoded `frontend/src/lib/sample-hackathons.ts` merged with `localStorage`, and submitting through `frontend/src/components/SubmitHackathonModal.tsx` only appends to local React state. This issue replaces the stub with a real, persistent CRUD API that matches the agreed data model and REST contract, so the frontend can stop relying on local-only data.

## Goal

Stand up a Flask API backed by a real datastore that persists hackathons across restarts and implements the core endpoints (`GET`/`POST`/`PATCH /api/hackathons`, single-item fetch, and the change-request endpoint) exactly as specified in the contract.

## Tasks

### Persistence
- [ ] Choose a datastore and record a short trade-off note in `backend/README.md`:
  - **SQLite** — simplest local dev, zero accounts/setup, single file (git-ignored); recommended default for this volunteer project.
  - **Firestore** — matches the originally floated "firebase (py)" idea, but needs a Google Cloud project, service-account credentials, and more setup.
  - The data model and contract are storage-agnostic, so this choice stays internal to the backend.
- [ ] Add the chosen driver(s) to `backend/requirements.txt` (e.g. nothing extra for stdlib `sqlite3`, or `firebase-admin` for Firestore).
- [ ] Define the storage layer for the `Hackathon` model (fields below) so data persists across server restarts.

### API endpoints (base path `/api`, JSON in/out, ISO 8601 dates)
- [ ] `GET /api/hackathons` — list `published` hackathons; support query params `?status=`, `?upcoming=true`, `?past=true`, `?tag=`, `?q=`, `?sort=date`.
- [ ] `GET /api/hackathons/:id` — return a single hackathon, or `404` with `{ "error": "..." }` if not found.
- [ ] `POST /api/hackathons` — submit a new hackathon. Validate that **at least one of `name` or `url`** is present (everything else optional); return the created resource plus its `status`. (AI validation that decides `published` vs `pending` is a separate issue — see Dependencies/Out of scope. For now, default new submissions to `published`, or `pending` behind a simple flag so the lifecycle wiring exists.)
- [ ] `PATCH /api/hackathons/:id` — edit fields on an existing hackathon; set `updatedAt`.
- [ ] `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` — create a reviewable **pending edit** (`status: "needs-changes"`) against a `published` hackathon; the live item is untouched until an admin/AI approves.
- [ ] On `PATCH` and `change-request`, expose a **validation hook point** that `ai-validation` fills in later (this issue only wires the seam; the AI decision logic itself is owned by `ai-validation`).

### Validation, config, CORS, seed
- [ ] Input validation: enforce the `name` OR `url` rule on create, reject unknown/invalid `status` and `mode` values, and validate date fields are ISO 8601. Return errors as `{ "error": string }` with proper HTTP codes (`400` for bad input, `404` for missing, etc.).
- [ ] Enable CORS for the frontend origin (Vite dev server, `http://localhost:5173`) so the React app can call the API; make the allowed origin configurable.
- [ ] Seed the datastore from the current sample data in `frontend/src/lib/sample-hackathons.ts`, mapping the old thin fields to the new model: `topic` → `name`, `date` → `startDate`, `prize` (boolean) → `hasPrize`, `link` → `url`, keep `prizeDetails`/`location`, and set `status: "published"`. An empty `location: ''` (as in `sample-5`) is normalized to an omitted/empty `location`, consistent with the `data-model` migration mapping.
- [ ] Add config/env handling for any secrets (e.g. Firestore credentials path, allowed CORS origin) — do not commit credentials; document required env vars in `backend/README.md`.
- [ ] Update `backend/README.md` with run instructions, the chosen-datastore note, env vars, and the new endpoint list (replacing the current `/health` + `/ping`-only docs).

## Canonical data model (align exactly — do not rename fields)

```
Hackathon {
  id: string
  name: string            // REQUIRED on a fully-formed record
  description?: string
  url?: string            // official link
  startDate?: string      // ISO 8601 date
  endDate?: string        // ISO 8601 date
  location?: string
  mode?: "in-person" | "online" | "hybrid"
  organizer?: string
  hasPrize?: boolean
  prizeDetails?: string
  tags?: string[]
  status: "draft" | "pending" | "published" | "needs-changes"
  submittedAt?: string    // ISO timestamp
  updatedAt?: string      // ISO timestamp
  interestCount?: number  // reserved, deferred
}
```

Submission rule: only **one of `{name, url}`** is required; everything else optional.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/hackathons` with only `name` (or only `url`) succeeds and returns the created resource with an `id` and a `status`; a body with neither returns `400` and `{ "error": "..." }`.
- [ ] `GET /api/hackathons` returns a JSON array of `published` items; `GET /api/hackathons/:id` returns the matching item or `404`.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/hackathons/:id` updates fields and reflects them on a subsequent `GET`.
- [ ] `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` against a published item creates a `needs-changes` pending edit without altering the live published record.
- [ ] All responses use the canonical field names, `status` values, and `/api/...` paths from the contract; dates are ISO 8601; errors are `{ "error": string }` with appropriate HTTP codes.
- [ ] Created/listed/fetched data **persists across a backend restart**.
- [ ] The seed populates the datastore with the five entries from `frontend/src/lib/sample-hackathons.ts` mapped to the new model.
- [ ] CORS allows requests from the frontend origin.
- [ ] `backend/README.md` documents how to run the backend, the datastore trade-off note, and required env vars.

## Dependencies

- **`data-model`** (expand the Hackathon type + define the REST contract) — this issue implements the server side of the model and endpoints it defines, so field names and status values must match. Build can proceed in parallel with the frontend wiring once the contract is agreed.

## Out of scope / notes

- **Q&A endpoints — OUT OF SCOPE.** The Q&A endpoints (`GET`/`POST /api/hackathons/:id/questions`, `POST /api/questions/:id/answers`) are owned by the Q&A issue (`qa-comments`), which holds the question/answer schema and threading detail. Do **not** implement them here.
- **`change-request` endpoint ownership.** The server-side implementation of `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` is owned by **this issue** (`backend-api`). The frontend "Suggest an edit" UI that calls it is owned by the `change-request` issue.
- **AI validation hook.** The logic that decides `published` vs `pending` on submit (and approves pending/needs-changes edits) lives in the `ai-validation` issue. Here, just wire the status field and expose the validation hook on `POST`/`PATCH`/`change-request` so the lifecycle exists (default `published`, or `pending` behind a flag); `ai-validation` adds the decision logic, not the endpoints themselves.
- The deferred `GET /api/hackathons/:id/interest` endpoint and `interestCount` population (via Discord) are **not** part of this issue.
- Suggested new label for tracking: a **`backend`** label would help filter server-side work. Only existing repo labels are applied to this issue; this is a recommendation for maintainers.
- Keep scope realistic: a single-file SQLite store with a thin storage module is perfectly acceptable for this volunteer student project — no ORM or microservice architecture required.

1. Create a free Supabase project. Save the **Project URL**, **anon key**, **service_role key**.
2. Create the table (note the extra map columns `lat`, `lng`, `geo_status`):
```sql
create table public.hackathons (
  id uuid primary key,
  host text not null,            -- company_name
  title text not null,
  url text not null,
  locations text[] not null default '{}',
  format text,                   -- In-Person | Virtual | Hybrid
  prize text,
  state text,                    -- open | opens_soon | closed
  active boolean default true,
  is_visible boolean default true,
  date_posted bigint,
  date_updated bigint,
  source text,
  lat double precision,          -- filled by geocoder (#12)
  lng double precision,
  geo_status text,               -- geocoded | virtual | failed
  synced_at timestamptz default now()
);
alter table public.hackathons enable row level security;
create policy "public read" on public.hackathons
  for select to anon using (is_visible = true);
```
3. Add repo secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions): `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`. The **anon** key goes to the frontend env (#14), not here.
4. Seed once from current `listings.json` to confirm the shape works.

> **Depends on:** #2, #5

## Background / Context

Once a hackathon is `published`, its details can go stale — the date slips, a venue changes, or a typo slips through. Right now there is no way for a visitor (or even the original submitter) to flag a correction; the only submission flow we have is `frontend/src/components/SubmitHackathonModal.tsx`, which creates brand-new entries and currently just appends to local React state. We want a lightweight "suggest an edit" path that proposes corrections to an existing published item **without overwriting the live data**. The cards rendered by `frontend/src/components/HackathonCard.tsx` (listed on `frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx`) are the natural place to surface this action.

## Goal

Add a "Suggest an edit" affordance on a published hackathon that opens a form prefilled with the current values and submits a change-request to `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request`, creating a reviewable pending edit (`status: "needs-changes"`) while the original stays live until an admin or AI approves it.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a **"Suggest an edit"** button on `frontend/src/components/HackathonCard.tsx` (and/or a hackathon detail view, if one exists by the time this is picked up) for items with `status: "published"`.
- [ ] Build a change-request form, prefilled with the hackathon's current values. Reuse the field set and validation patterns from `frontend/src/components/SubmitHackathonModal.tsx` rather than inventing a new form. Editable fields should map to the canonical model: `name`, `description`, `url`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `location`, `mode`, `organizer`, `hasPrize`, `prizeDetails`, `tags`.
- [ ] On submit, call `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` with the proposed field values (JSON in/out, ISO 8601 dates). This endpoint creates a reviewable pending edit and does **not** mutate the live `published` record.
- [ ] Show clear success / error feedback after submission (e.g. "Thanks — your suggested edit is pending review"). Surface API errors returned as `{ error: string }`.
- [ ] Ensure the original published hackathon continues to render unchanged on `frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx` immediately after a change-request is submitted.
- [ ] Backend implementation of `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` is owned by **backend-api**; this issue owns ONLY the frontend Suggest-an-edit form + wiring and consumes that endpoint (mock it until the backend lands). Agree on the request payload shape and the returned resource with the backend-api issue before merging.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A "Suggest an edit" button is visible on a `published` hackathon (card and/or detail view).
- [ ] Clicking it opens a form **prefilled** with that hackathon's current field values.
- [ ] Submitting the form sends `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` and the user sees a clear success confirmation (or a readable error on failure).
- [ ] The submitted change-request results in a reviewable pending edit with `status: "needs-changes"` (verifiable via the backend / storage once that half exists).
- [ ] The original `published` hackathon stays live and unchanged until an admin or AI approves the edit — submitting a change-request never overwrites live data.

## Dependencies

- **data-model** — this feature relies on the canonical field names (`name`, `url`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `mode`, `hasPrize`, `tags`, etc.) and the `status` lifecycle value `"needs-changes"`.
- **backend-api** — owns the server implementation of `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request`, CORS for the frontend origin, and the pending-edit persistence. The backend owns the endpoint; this issue owns only the frontend "Suggest an edit" form + wiring that consumes it.

(Issue numbers don't exist yet — referenced by key.)

## Out of scope / notes

- **Admin review UI** (approving / rejecting pending edits, diffing proposed vs. live values) is out of scope here — this issue only covers *submitting* a change-request. An on-site admin review surface is a known follow-up tracked at the data-model level, not in this issue.
- **AI validation of change-requests** is optional and lives in the **ai-validation** issue. If the backend wires AI validation into `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` via its validation hook point, this frontend can simply consume whatever `status` comes back; no extra frontend work is required to enable it.
- `frontend/src/pages/Feedback.tsx` (the localStorage form with a "Previous Submissions" list) is a good reference for form layout, success messaging, and listing prior submissions — reuse that pattern where it fits.
- Until the backend endpoint exists, this can be developed against a stubbed/mocked `POST /api/hackathons/:id/change-request` so the frontend and backend can progress in parallel.
- Suggested new labels for triage (not in the repo label set yet, so not applied here): **frontend**, **backend**. Add them via repo settings if the team wants finer-grained filtering.

Part of #3375.

## Idea
A search type that ranks results by **graph importance** (PageRank / degree / betweenness centrality) rather than vector similarity alone — surfacing the hub entities of the graph or of a query-relevant subgraph. Great for "what are the key entities/themes here?" and for higher-quality global summaries.

## Why
All current ranking is vector-distance or feedback-weight based. Structural importance is a different, complementary signal we don't expose. (We already store node/edge **frequency** weights — a cheap degree-like proxy — but no centrality search type uses them.)

## Implementation
- New `SearchType.CENTRALITY` (optionally a `mode`: pagerank | degree | betweenness).
- Two viable routes:
  1. **In-memory:** project the relevant subgraph (existing `CogneeGraph`/`get_graph_data`) and compute centrality with networkx — portable across all backends.
  2. **Native:** Neo4j GDS `gds.pageRank` where available (fast path).
- Optionally scope to a query-seeded neighborhood first (reuse seed-resolution + `get_neighborhood`), then rank within it.
- Retriever returns top-ranked nodes/triplets (+ optional LLM summary). Consider exposing the existing `get_node_frequency_weights` as the cheap default.

## Acceptance
- `recall(query, query_type=SearchType.CENTRALITY)` returns entities ordered by structural importance within the query-relevant subgraph (or globally if no query anchor).
- In-memory path works on every backend; native GDS used where present.

Files: new centrality helper (in-memory networkx and/or `neo4j_metrics_utils`), `SearchType.py`, `modules/retrieval/`, `get_search_type_retriever_instance.py`.

Part of #3389.

## Idea
A task that detects **contradictory** facts in memory, links the outdated one to the newer one with a `supersedes` edge, and demotes the stale claim so retrieval prefers current truth. This is the "self-correcting wiki" move several hackathon teams built by hand (SUPERSEDES edges, retired claims) — make it a first-class memory task. Missing today.

## Design
- Detect conflicts: for entities/claims on the same subject (shared neighborhood or shared entity), use `LLMGateway` to judge whether two statements contradict; prefer the more recent (`created_at`/`updated_at`) or higher-feedback one.
- Resolve: add a `supersedes` edge from the newer claim to the older; demote the superseded node's `feedback_weight` (and optionally exclude it from default retrieval).
- Config: `confidence_threshold`, `prefer` (recency | feedback), `dry_run`.

## Notes / gaps
- There's **no bitemporal `valid_from`/`valid_to`** on nodes/edges — consider adding lightweight validity fields to `DataPoint`/edges as part of this, or encode supersession purely via the `supersedes` edge + weight demotion to start.
- Edge writes via `add_edge`; weight demotion via `set_node_feedback_weights`.

## Acceptance
- Given two contradictory claims, the task adds a `supersedes` edge and demotes the stale one; a subsequent recall surfaces the current claim.
- `dry_run` reports detected contradictions without mutating the graph.
title: [hackathon] Memory task: RECONCILE / supersede (contradiction resolution)

Part of #3389.

## Idea
A task that finds entities that are clearly related but **not yet linked**, and adds inferred edges — so the graph gets richer the more it's enriched, not just at extraction time. Missing today.

## Design
- Candidate generation: for each entity, pull near neighbors by embedding similarity (vector engine) and by **shared-entity overlap** (reuse the scorer in `tasks/memify/global_context_index/bucketing/graph/scoring.py`), restricted to pairs with no existing edge (`has_edge`).
- Relation inference: use `LLMGateway` to decide whether a real relationship exists and label it; only above a confidence threshold.
- Write inferred edges via `add_edges`, tagged (e.g. `inferred=True`, lower initial `feedback_weight`) so they're distinguishable and prunable.
- Config: `similarity_threshold`, `max_new_edges_per_node`, `confidence_threshold`, `dry_run`.

## Notes
- Primitives ready: `get_filtered_graph_data` (pull Entities), `get_neighborhood`, `add_edge(s)`, vector search, `LLMGateway`.
- Keep it idempotent (skip pairs already linked or already inferred).

## Acceptance
- On a graph with obviously-related-but-unlinked entities, the task proposes correct edges; `dry_run` lists them without writing.
- Inferred edges are tagged and don't duplicate existing relationships.
